description: The Census of Agriculture is the complete count of US farms and ranches and the people who operate them, including places that sold or would normally sell at least $1,000 of agricultural products. It covers land use and ownership, operator characteristics, production practices, crops and livestock, and income and expenditures. It is conducted by the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) every five years; the 2022 census was released on 13 February 2024 and the next is due for 2027. Results are published for the nation, states, counties and congressional districts through the Quick Stats database, downloadable data files, state and county profiles and reports, free of charge. Caveats: only aggregated data are released, because NASS must keep individual responses confidential, so some county cells are withheld, and the five-year interval means rapid changes are missed. For simulation it provides county-level exposure data on farms, crops, livestock, irrigation and farm income for hazard exposure and resilience analyses of droughts, floods and supply disruptions, and for capacity planning of rural water, energy and transport infrastructure. It is related to the USDA NASS Quick Stats record in this catalogue, which serves the census tables alongside the annual surveys.
